description: resolve_store_name: ignoreCwd -> cwd shape -> nameOverrides -> git -> directory name -> validation -> existing names -> CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME. A case without `git` asserts that git is not consulted.

cases.note: git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir in this repository (git 2.50.1, 2026-09-02).
VibeDub/server -> VibeDub/.git; matches the real link pair -Volumes-…-VibeDub-server -> VibeDub. Recorded 2026-09-02.
VibeIDEA/vibe-plugins/vibe-agent is a plain subdirectory of the superproject (real link pair -> VibeIDEA); the submodule lives deeper. Recorded 2026-09-02.

Absorbed submodule of VibeIDEA (.gitmodules path = vibe-plugins/vibe-agent/resources/vibeDefaults, upstream VibeBrains): common dir under .git/modules/, pointer file is relative. Name = last component; a standalone clone of the same upstream would be `VibeBrains`. Recorded 2026-09-02.
Subdirectory `design/` of the submodule: same common dir, nearest .git is the submodule's pointer file found above. Recorded 2026-09-02.
git worktree add ../linked-wt: common dir is the main repository's .git; the pointer names .git/worktrees/linked-wt. Recorded 2026-09-02.
Subdirectory of the linked worktree: identical outcome. Recorded 2026-09-02.
git worktree add --relative-paths (git 2.48+): the pointer is relative to the worktree. Recorded 2026-09-02.
A worktree created from inside a submodule: gitdir ends with modules/libs/foo/worktrees/subwt; dropping the worktrees pair yields the submodule's git dir. Recorded 2026-09-02.
Worktree created on the Windows machine, opened on macOS: git fails (not a git repository), but the pointer file names the repository. Real file content, 2026-09-02.
Subdirectory of that worktree: the pointer is found above. Recorded 2026-09-02.
If git refused the submodule, its relative pointer still names it (real pointer content).
A pointer file without a gitdir: line.
`gitdir:` with nothing after it.
git init --separate-git-dir: the pointer and the common dir name a directory that is neither .git nor under .git/modules. Recorded 2026-09-02.
Same pointer with git refusing: still not a recognizable layout.
Inside a bare repository the common dir is the repository itself. Recorded 2026-09-02.
inner/.git/HEAD contains garbage: git 2.50.1 silently resolves the OUTER repository with exit 0. The nearest .git disagrees, so no name. Recorded 2026-09-02.
An empty .git directory is skipped by git discovery the same way. Recorded 2026-09-02.

GIT_DIR pointing elsewhere makes git answer with a foreign repository (the CLI strips GIT_* before spawning; the core still refuses). `lone/.git` is an empty directory; without any `.git` the answer is the same and the core still refuses (commonDirWithoutDotGit). Recorded 2026-09-02.
Contract: the core does not resolve symlinks. git prints physical paths, so a logical cwd (`/tmp`, not `/private/tmp`) mismatches; the hook resolves cwd once before everything.

Directory created as NFD `cafe<U+0301>`, entered through its NFC spelling: git 2.50.1 prints the NFD form (also with core.precomposeunicode=true) while the CLI reports cwd in NFC. Components compare after NFC, the name is NFC. Recorded 2026-09-02.
A submodule whose path in the superproject ends in `worktrees/<name>`: the pointer is read both ways and the reading that equals git's common dir wins.
git answered but no .git entry exists above cwd: the answer cannot be explained.
A .git directory exists but git failed (dubious ownership, corruption): never fall back to the directory name.
git could not be run: no transport without git, no naming either.
The .git walk did not complete: never treat as 'no repository'.
A wrapper leaving CR/LF or spaces in stdout must not change the layout.
A repository whose root is the filesystem root has no name.
VibeSweep is not a repository: exit 128, no .git above (discovery stops at the /Volumes mount). Recorded 2026-09-02.
A trailing separator does not change the name.
cwd `/` (VibeDub runner) without an ignore rule: an error, never a store named root. git is not consulted. Recorded 2026-09-02.
The owner's rule for the runner (architecture §9): `/` is ignored before the root check.
Drive root ignored by its `/`-form literal.
UNC share root ignored; the pattern is written with `/` separators.
The same root without a trailing slash in the pattern: patterns are canonicalized like the cwd.
An empty cwd is relative, not a root.
`.` is relative.
`D:` without a root is drive-relative.
A drive-relative cwd is rejected before ignore patterns are consulted and renders without `/`, so an absolute pattern cannot match it.
Drive root on Windows.
UNC share root without trailing separator (typed-path reports it as not absolute; the prefix alone anchors it).
Relative cwd.
`D:foo` is relative to the drive's current directory.
Git for Windows prints forward slashes; the .git walk reports backslashes; both name one location.
Backslashes in the git output as well.
cwd typed in lower case, git answers in canonical case: locations compare without regard to case, the name follows git.
Submodule layout on Windows.
A submodule inside a submodule keeps git's literal `modules` segments; the name is still the last component.
A literal pattern matches exactly; git is not consulted.
`/**` matches descendants.
`foo/**` does not match `foo` itself (globset semantics): the base needs its own literal pattern.
`/a/b` does not match `/a/bc`.
An override wins over a repository; git is not consulted.
Two overrides matching one cwd: an error, not 'longest wins'.
Windows patterns match without regard to case.
POSIX patterns are byte-exact: the lower-case key does not match, git decides.
A POSIX pattern never matches a Windows cwd.
`/**` ignores a subtree.
`*` does not cross `/` (literal_separator).
A literal pattern is not a prefix.
The cwd is rendered without its trailing separator before matching.
Windows pattern vs lower-case backslash cwd.
When both match, ignore wins: a contradictory config does nothing.
The reported pattern is the first match in file order.
A directory named CON cannot be checked out on Windows.
Windows reserves the stem before the first dot: aux.js.
A project directory literally named .git.
NTFS drops trailing dots.
Colon is forbidden on NTFS.
An existing store differing only by case is the same store: its spelling is reused.
Two existing spellings of one key: the store is already broken; refuse.
NFD name vs existing NFC store: one store.
Names derived from paths are NFC: the same directory yields one spelling whichever machine derives it first.
The same spelling listed twice (tree plus working copy) is not a collision.
Windows also reserves COM¹ (superscript digit) per Microsoft documentation.
A pattern with a trailing separator matches the cwd without it; the reported pattern is the text as written.
Same tolerance for overrides.
A literal `[work]` component is matched through a character class.
Overrides are reconciled with existing names too.
Desktop sets CLAUDE_CODE_PROJECT_DIR_NAME=session for 3p sessions (hooksLifecycle): the project directory is shared by every cwd, so nothing is linked. Recorded 2026-09-02.
Plan B: the variable equals the store name, so projects/<name> can be linked directly.
Equality with the store is by identity key (case-folded): projects/vibememory -> store VibeMemory is still plan B.
CLI 2.1.255 silently ignores a value outside [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64} (run 2026-09-02: `Weird Name.x` -> directory by the formula), so the engine ignores it too and links normally.
CLI 2.1.255 silently ignores a reserved device name (run 2026-09-02: `aux`).
65 characters exceed the CLI's {1,64} rule (2.1.255 strings).
